title: Object Detection: YOLO Geometry and NMS

questions.question: What coordinate convention does validate_boxes enforce?
options: Normalized center-width-height boxes with values only in [0,1]
Integer corner pixels with x2<=x1 allowed for a point
Finite absolute xyxy boxes with x1<x2 and y1<y2
Four logits that have not yet been decoded
questions.explanation: The local geometry APIs use absolute corners and require a positive width and height; normalization is not silently assumed.

questions.question: What is the IoU of [0,0,10,10] and [5,0,15,10]?
questions.explanation: The intersection area is 50 and the union is 100+100-50=150, giving 50/150 = 1/3.

questions.question: In encode(box, cell_x, cell_y, stride, anchor), what do tx and ty represent?
options: Logits for the center offsets within the selected cell
The absolute pixel coordinates of the box's top-left corner
The anchor's width and height in pixels
The class index and confidence threshold
questions.explanation: The center divided by stride gives a cell-relative offset, which encode maps through a logit so decode(sigmoid(...)) can recover it.

questions.question: What does assign_targets set for the chosen anchor at an object's cell?
options: Every anchor's objectness to one and all class bits to one
Objectness one and one selected class bit, along with four encoded box values
Only the absolute xyxy box; no class target is stored
A probability distribution produced by a trained model
questions.explanation: The target row contains encoded center/size, objectness 1, and a one-hot class vector for the best width/height anchor.

questions.question: Why does yolo_loss use a separate no-objectness component?
options: It replaces all coordinate regression for positive cells
It makes every empty cell a background class in the class vector
Most grid/anchor locations have no assigned object and need an explicit negative objectness term
It is needed only when boxes contain NaN coordinates
questions.explanation: The boolean object mask separates positive and negative objectness examples; the shape and finite-value checks still apply to the full tensor.

questions.question: How does nms resolve equal scores for overlapping boxes?
options: It keeps the box with the largest class ID regardless of overlap
It averages all overlapping coordinates into one class-free box
It randomizes the order so ties cannot be observed
It keeps the lower original index first, then suppresses later boxes above the IoU threshold
questions.explanation: The lexsort key is descending score followed by original index, making tie handling deterministic before IoU suppression.
